title: Financial liquidity: ratios, working capital, and automation
summary: Learn what financial liquidity is, how to calculate current, quick, and cash ratios, and how automation keeps liquidity metrics aligned with live cash.
body_markdown:
# Financial liquidity: ratios, working capital, and automation


**Financial liquidity** is the ability to meet short-term obligations without breaking operations. Classic ratios (current, quick, and cash) come from the balance sheet; real liquidity shows up in the cash calendar, aging, and commitments the balance sheet does not yet show.


A “good” month-end ratio can hide clustered maturities next week. That is why liquidity needs both the statement and treasury:[cash management](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/gestao-de-caixa) ,[cash conversion](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/conversao-de-caixa) , and[leverage](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/endividamento) .


## What financial liquidity is


Usual ratios:


- **Current ratio:** current assets / current liabilities.
- **Quick ratio:** (current assets − inventory) / current liabilities.
- **Cash ratio:** cash and equivalents / current liabilities.


They measure structural headroom. They do not replace treasury's question: “do we have money in the right account on the right date?”.


Working capital (current assets − current liabilities) is the fuel for that headroom. If the operating cycle lengthens, accounting liquidity can look stable while cash tightens.


## Why it matters


Weak liquidity creates:


- late suppliers and lost discounts;
- emergency use of expensive lines;
- covenant risk;
- hiring and CAPEX freezes.


Idle excess liquidity also has a cost: spread left on the table and diluted ROIC. The point is policy, not “more is always better”.


## How it works in practice with automation


1. The balance sheet feeds official ratios at close.
2. Banks and open items feed liquidity over the next 13 weeks.
3. Rules alert when a ratio or cash floor is breached.
4. Slow-moving inventory is highlighted in the quick ratio.
5. FP&A crosses liquidity with[scenarios](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/cenarios-base-otimista-pessimista) .
6. The exec pack shows the ratio plus the cash gap, not one or the other.


The[cash flow solution](https://www.abstra.io/en/solutions/finance-automation/cash-flow-and-reporting) covers the operating leg;[indicator analysis](https://www.abstra.io/en/solutions/finance-automation/fpa/indicator-analysis) covers the management leg.


## Applied example


A manufacturer reported a 1.6x current ratio. Underneath, 40% of current assets was slow inventory and 30% of the fortnight's payments clustered on two days. The ratio calmed the board; treasury did not sleep.


With automation, the dashboard showed current ratio, projected cash ratio, and the maturity map. The committee pulled a line forward and accelerated liquidation of stuck stock.


## Manual vs automated


Step Manual process Automated process


Ratios Calculated at close Official formulas in the management pack


Near-term cash Treasury spreadsheet Connected position and forecast


Asset quality Inventory “by feel” Turns and aging visible


Alert After the squeeze Before clustered due dates


Scenario Off-cycle Liquidity downside in the same model


## How to implement


1. Set policy: cash-ratio floor and cash floor.
2. Document what enters each ratio.
3. Unite balance sheet, banks, and open items.
4. Qualify current assets (aging and turns).
5. Link liquidity to covenants and[leverage](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/endividamento) .
6. Review in the same treasury and FP&A forum.


## When it makes sense to automate


It makes sense with multiple entities, seasonality, covenants, or when the ratio and cash tell different stories. Simple structures can calculate the ratio at close and run cash on a short cycle.


## Common mistakes


- celebrating the current ratio with stuck inventory;
- watching the month and ignoring the week;
- treating investments as operating cash without a rule;
- leaving doubtful receivables in the ratio;
- a liquidity policy nobody monitors.


## Checklist


- Is there a cash floor and a cash-ratio floor?
- Do ratios have an official formula?
- Are customer and inventory aging visible?
- Do treasury and FP&A use the same base?
- Do covenants enter the alert?
- Is liquidity downside modeled?


## FAQ


### Which liquidity ratio should we watch first?


Cash ratio (or a cash floor) for treasury; current and quick for the board. All three together prevent false comfort.


### Does high liquidity mean health?


Not by itself. It can be idle capital. Cross it with[ROIC](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/o-que-e-roic) and CCC.


### How often should we update?


Balance-sheet ratios at close; position and forecast on a short cycle (daily or weekly). Automation allows both without two worlds.


### How does automation help liquidity?


It does not create cash. It flags the gap early, speeds collections, organizes payments, and makes the ratio auditable. See[accounts receivable](https://www.abstra.io/en/solutions/finance-automation/accounts-receivable) and[cash flow](https://www.abstra.io/en/solutions/finance-automation/cash-flow-and-reporting) .


## Conclusion


Financial liquidity is structural headroom plus a real calendar. Automating ratios and treasury on the same base avoids the classic “the balance sheet looks fine, cash does not”.
